key_insight: PC-Dr.DPO makes test-time learning more conservative when majority-vote pseudo-labels are sensitive to finite sampling, without claiming to correct population-majority bias.
engineering_relevance: The approach targets more reliable adaptation of pretrained language models to unlabeled domains by moderating uncertain updates and reducing self-supervised forgetting.
method: Decompose majority-vote error into population-majority bias and prompt-dependent finite-rollout variation.
Condition within-prompt robust DPO reweighting on observed vote reliability.
Use a cache-based mechanism to reduce forgetting during online adaptation.
evidence_signal: Across six mathematical and knowledge-intensive reasoning benchmarks and five model backbones, PC-Dr.DPO matches or outperforms the strongest TTRL baseline in 24 of 30 settings.
watch_item: Population-majority bias is generally unidentifiable without external supervision, so stable majority votes can still yield incorrect pseudo-labels.
paper_title: On the Reliability of Majority-Vote Pseudo-Labels in Test-Time Reinforcement Learning
